note: Draft vectors for LIP-0021. No vector reads a chain: scripts, heights and histories are stated, and no node decoded or validated them. Keys are the compressed forms of published BIP-340 test keys and belong to nobody. Names, values, hashes and the octets of signatures are placeholders, and no signature in this file verifies. A refused vector holds one defect and names a valid neighbour that differs from it in that defect; a vector marked compound holds two findings and names none. No verdict of this file records a closure.

fields.scripts: script_hex is a whole output script. confirmed_at is the height of the block that holds the output; it is stated where the address script is a witness key hash, the one script whose reading depends on it. expect.prefix is update, registration, reservation or none; name and value are the pushed octets as ASCII; expect.reading is the outcome of O3.4 against pin.
fields.writers: created states the operation and the name of the output whose writer is asked. inputs lists, for each input of that operation, the script of the output that it spends, its unlocking script and, where it has one, the items of its witness; spent_confirmed_at is the height of the block that holds the spent output and is stated where that output is a witness key hash.
fields.walks: history lists the outputs of a name from the current one back. prefix is update, registration or none (no supported prefix); reading is the outcome of O3.4 against the pin of the rule; swarma stands for the octets of the `swarma` member of the value, and none for a value without the member; writer is the outcome of O4.4 for the operation that created the output; readable false means that the node does not supply the transaction of the output. context.step_bound is the operator's bound of O6.3; context.transaction_index false is a node without the index.

rules.title: the verifier's own node and the three kinds of fact
rules.not_covered: No vector reads a node. The vectors of O1.3 state that a fact is missing.

rules.title: one consistent observation
rules.not_covered: No vector takes an observation or holds a pending operation. The observation profile is open.

rules.title: a missing fact proves nothing
the form and the point of an owner pin
the pin is the key itself
comparison with a signing key by x coordinate
the verifier parses the octets itself
rules.not_covered: No vector shows what a node decodes. script-28 holds a script that the node's parser reads otherwise than this profile, by the source of that parser.

rules.title: three supported prefixes
two supported address scripts
three outcomes of a reading
unsupported proves nothing
the name input of an operation
written by the pinned owner
the hash type in the unlocking script or in the witness
three outcomes of the writer check
a live name
an expired name and a new registration
rules.not_covered: The vectors show that an expired name refuses and that a walk from a new registration ends there. None shows a chain on which a name expires and is registered again.

rules.title: the steps of a walk
the output current at a block, and the stretch
a walk that cannot be finished
caching
after a reorganisation
the issuer's name at admission
a recipient by name at admission
a notary's name
rules.not_covered: No vector of a notary's name holds two findings, a checkpoint outside the active chain, or a name without a live output.

rules.title: the consent of a recipient by name
a change that the owner signed
rules.not_covered: No vector holds a pending operation or a closure. The readings that the rule names are in the groups scripts and writers.

valid.claim: A compressed key. Its first octet states the parity of y.
The key with the same x coordinate and the other parity. It is a pin, of another key.

invalid.claim: The x coordinate alone, 64 characters: the form of a signing key and not of a pin.
The uncompressed form of the same key, 65 octets.
A first octet of 04 before 32 octets.
The hash of the key, 20 octets, in the place of the key.
66 characters of which one is no hexadecimal digit.
A first octet of 02 before a value that is no x coordinate of a point of the curve.
The same value after a first octet of 03.

comparisons.claim: A pin and the signing key with its x coordinate are the same key.
The pin of the other parity and the same signing key are the same key as well: the comparison ignores the first octet.
A pin and a signing key with another x coordinate.

The same script in the block of height 475000, the first in which the main chain enforces the witness rules.
The script of script-01 read against the pin of the other parity: the hash commits to the first octet of the key.
An update that pays the hash of the uncompressed form of the pinned key.
An update that pays the hash of another key.
An update that pays the witness key hash of another key.
The script of script-10 one block lower, at height 474999: the main chain did not enforce the witness rules there, and anybody could spend the output.
A script hash behind the prefix.
A script hash that wraps the witness key hash of the pinned key.
A witness script hash behind the prefix.
A Taproot output for the x coordinate of the pinned key behind the prefix.
The pinned key itself, without a hash, behind the prefix.
One of two keys, the pinned key among them, behind the prefix.
The key hash of script-01 with one more opcode after it.
A hash of 19 octets in the frame of the key hash.
A witness program of 19 octets.
The 20 octets of the pinned key after a witness version of 1 in place of 0.

A prefix with nothing after it.

The script of script-01 with one OP_NOP between the prefix and the address script. By its source the node's parser skips the opcode and finds the address script of script-01; under this profile the address script begins with that opcode and is unsupported.
The name is pushed with 4c although it has fewer than 76 octets.
A value of 13 octets is pushed with 4d.
A value of 300 octets is pushed with 4e and a length of four octets.
The opcode of an update before one push only.
The opcode of an update before the three pushes of a registration.
A registration that ends with 6d 75 in place of 6d 6d.
An update whose two last opcodes stand in the other order, 75 6d.
A reservation with a hash of 19 octets.
The script of script-01 cut off inside the push of the value.
The address script of script-01 without any prefix: an ordinary output of the pinned key and no output of a name.
An empty script.

writers.claim: An update. Its second input spends the previous output of the name, a key hash that the pin controls, with a signature that ends in 01. Its first input pays the fee with a coin of another key. The octets of the signatures are placeholders.
A registration whose name input spends a reservation that the pin controls.
The first update after a registration: its name input spends the registration output.
An update whose name input spends a witness key hash that the pin controls. The unlocking script is empty, and the witness holds the signature, which ends in 01, and the key.
An update whose name input spends an output of another key, signed by that key: a transfer to the pinned owner, whose value the earlier holder wrote.
A registration by another party. The reservation is that party's; the pinned owner signed a fee input beside it, and a fee input is no name input.
An update whose name input spends the witness key hash of another key.
The update of writer-01 with the hash type 81, SIGHASH_ALL with ANYONECANPAY.
The update of writer-01 with the hash type 03, SIGHASH_SINGLE.
The update of writer-01 with the hash type 02, SIGHASH_NONE.
The update of writer-01 with the hash type 83, SIGHASH_SINGLE with ANYONECANPAY.
The update of writer-01 with the hash type 00: every octet but 01 is outside the profile, whatever a node makes of it.
The name input spends an output of the name whose address script is a script hash.
The unlocking script of the name input has three pushes.
The signature of the name input is pushed with 4c although it has fewer than 76 octets.
The second push of the unlocking script is another key than the pin. A node does not validate such a spend of this output; a reader that meets it concludes nothing.
The name input spends a key hash with an empty unlocking script and no witness.
The name input spends a key hash as writer-01 does and carries a witness beside its unlocking script.
No input spends an output with a supported prefix: the previous output of the name pushes its name with 4c.
The only input with a supported prefix carries another name. Consensus does not allow such an update; a reader that meets it finds no name input.
The update of writer-04 with the hash type 81 in the witness.
The update of writer-04 with a witness of three items.
The update of writer-04 with the signature and the key in an unlocking script, as for a key hash, and no witness. A node does not validate such a spend of a witness key hash.
The update of writer-04 where the spent output is confirmed at height 474999, below the height from which the main chain enforces the witness rules.

live.claim: The block of the operation itself.
The last block at which the name is live, 35999 blocks above the operation.
One block later the name is expired.
A regression test chain, whose depth is 30: 29 blocks above the operation.
The same chain one block later.

walks.claim: The walk ends at the bound registration. The output that was current at the recent block (o2, height 400) and the two later outputs are controlled and carry the bound `swarma`.
One more update above the recent block that changes neither the owner nor `swarma`: a renewal, or an update of another member of the value. It closes nothing.
The current output reads as another key: the name is in other hands.

The name changed hands and came back: the current output is controlled again, and an earlier output of the stretch is not. The walk finds it without any memory of an earlier observation; a check of the current owner alone passes it.
An output of the stretch carries another `swarma`: the grant key was replaced. The notary rule passes the same history (walk-notary-01).
An output before the stretch belonged to another key. The stretch starts at the output that was current at the recent block, and what lies before it is not judged.
The walk ends at another registration than the bound one: the name expired and was registered again, by the same owner key and with the same `swarma`.
The name is expired at the tip: its current output is 36000 blocks below it.
One block earlier the name is live.
The bound registration is confirmed above the recent block: no output of it was current at that block.
An output of the stretch is unsupported. Nothing is proved, and the refusal is not that of a change.
The verifier bounds a walk at three steps, and the registration is five steps back. The stretch itself was read and shows no change; the registration was not reached.
The node keeps no transaction index and supplies no transaction.
A bound of five steps is exactly the length of the walk.
Two findings: an output in view reads as another key (row 2), and a later one is unsupported (row 5). The change that the chain proved is reported.

The value of the current output was written by another party. The issuer rule in force does not ask who wrote the value and passes; the extension of section 4.1 would refuse, and the notary rule refuses the same history (walk-notary-04).
An output before the stretch has an unsupported address script. The walk needs its prefix and nothing else.
An output before the stretch has no supported prefix, and the walk cannot pass it.
The node does not supply the transaction of one output before the stretch, while every other read works.
An output of the stretch carries a value without a `swarma` member.

Two findings: an output in view reads as another key (row 2), and a bound of three steps ends the walk before the registration (row 5). The change is reported although the walk was cut short behind it.
Two findings: an output in view reads as another key (row 2), and the bound registration is confirmed above the recent block (row 4).
Two findings: the bound registration is confirmed above the recent block (row 4), and an output in view is unsupported (row 5).
The output that was current at the recent block (o2) reads as another key, and every later output is controlled: at the block that the grant commits, the name was in other hands.
An output that is confirmed in the recent block itself (o3, height 500) was current at that block. The output before it belonged to another key and lies before the stretch.
The same history with the recent block one lower. o3 is now confirmed above it, and the output that was current at it is o2, which reads as another key.
Two findings: the name is expired at the tip (row 1), and the node supplies no transaction (row 5). The expiry needs no walk and is reported.

The owner paid the name to an unsupported script (o3) and replaced that output later (o4). For a grant whose recent block lies below the replacement, the unsupported output stays in view, and the grant refuses.
The same history for a grant whose recent block is the block of the replacement (o4, height 700): the unsupported output lies before the stretch.
The current output is controlled by the owner key that the grant signs. An earlier output belonged to another key; the rule does not read it.
The current output reads as another key.
The current output is unsupported.
The name is expired at the tip.
The node does not supply the transaction of the current output.
The evidence output (o2, height 400) was current at the recent block: the output that spends it (o3) is confirmed above that block.
The evidence output is the current output of the name.
The evidence output was replaced below the recent block: o1 was spent by o2 at height 400.
The evidence output is confirmed above the recent block.
The evidence output is no output of the name: the walk reaches the registration without meeting it.
The evidence output reads as another key.
The name was expired at the recent block: the evidence output is 36000 blocks below it.
The verifier bounds a walk at two steps, and the evidence output is the third output of the walk.
The evidence output is unsupported. The code is the same as for a condition that fails.
The evidence output is confirmed in the recent block itself (o3, height 500).
The output that spends the evidence output (o2) is confirmed in the recent block itself, so the evidence output was no longer current at that block.
The evidence output is the registration itself, and the first update of the name is confirmed above the recent block.

The stretch from the checkpoint is controlled by the bound owner, and the owner wrote the value of the current output. `swarma` changed on the stretch, which the notary rule allows: the attestation key was rotated. The issuer rule refuses the same history (walk-issuer-05).
An output of the stretch reads as another key.
The bound registration is confirmed above the checkpoint.
The operation that created the current output was not authorized by the bound owner: another key held its name input. The issuer rule in force passes the same history (walk-issuer-16).
The plain history: the stretch from the checkpoint is controlled by the bound owner, and the owner wrote the value of the current output.
The name input of the operation that created the current output was signed with a hash type outside the profile. Nothing is proved.
An output of the stretch is unsupported.
The registration is the current output, and the bound owner signed it: its name input, a reservation, was the owner's.
The registration is the current output, and its reservation was another party's: the owner received the name and wrote nothing.
The walk ends at another registration than the bound one: the name expired and was registered again by the same owner key.
